matter_reference_date_basis: exam_session "APRIL 2020" recorded in candidates/matters/M076.json; the law is taken as it stood in April 2020, so the Notaries (Amendment) Acts No. 31 of 2022 and No. 6 of 2024 and the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Acts No. 30 of 2022 and No. 4 of 2024 all post-date the matter.
corpus_gaps: No statute in the corpus prescribes the form or the words of a testimonium clause. The testimonium is a conveyancing and notarial precedent form derived from practice; the statutes fix only what the clause must contain (place, date in letters, who signs, how many parts).

Form E of the Second Schedule to the Notaries Ordinance (the prescribed attestation form) is not held as a separate section in the corpus; it is reachable only through the reference in s.31(21). Form E in any event governs the attestation, which follows the signatures, not the testimonium.

The corpus holds only the current consolidated text of Notaries Ordinance s.31 and Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2. The April 2020 text had to be reconstructed by subtracting the amending sections 31-2022/s16, 6-2024/s3, 30-2022/s2 and 4-2024/s2; no as-at-2020 snapshot exists in the corpus.

Stamp duty payable on an indenture of lease (Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006 and the gazetted rate orders) was not pursued: the rate schedules are not extracted, and stamp duty is recited in the notary's attestation under s.31(20)(f), not in the testimonium.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: He shall correctly insert in letters in every deed or instrument executed before him the day, month, and year on which and the place where the same is executed, and shall sign the same.
provisions.why_relevant: This is the statutory source of the two variable elements every testimonium clause carries: the place of execution and the date of execution, and the requirement that the date be written in letters rather than figures. A testimonium that gave the date in numerals, or omitted the place, would put the attesting notary in breach of rule (18).
provisions.temporal_note: Rule (18) was not touched by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 47 of 2011, No. 31 of 2022 or No. 6 of 2024; the text quoted is the text in force in April 2020.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless the person executing the same and the witnesses shall have signed the same in his presence and in the presence of one another, and unless he shall have signed the same in the presence of the executant and of the attesting witnesses.
provisions.why_relevant: The testimonium is the clause by which the deed itself records the act of signing that rule (12) requires: the parties setting their hands to the instrument at one place, on one date, before the notary and the witnesses. It fixes the single time and place the testimonium must recite.
provisions.temporal_note: Rule (12) was not amended by the 2011, 2022 or 2024 amending Acts; text as in force in April 2020.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument to which at least two witnesses have not subscribed their signatures in letters.
provisions.why_relevant: Explains why the execution block that immediately follows the testimonium carries two witness signature lines. It shapes the layout the testimonium leads into, but the clause itself speaks of the parties setting their hands, not of the witnesses.
provisions.temporal_note: Rule (8) unamended by the 2011, 2022 and 2024 amending Acts; in force in April 2020.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: He shall carefully preserve as his protocol a draft or copy of every deed or instrument executed or acknowledged before him, to which shall be attached his signature and those of the party and witnesses to the original deed or instrument
provisions.why_relevant: The protocol is one of the two further parts the parties sign. Together with the duplicate required by rule (26) it is the statutory reason a Sri Lankan testimonium says the parties set their hands hereto and to two others of the same tenor and date as these presents.
provisions.temporal_note: Rule (24) unamended by the 2011, 2022 and 2024 amending Acts; in force in April 2020.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: He shall deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which he resides the following documents, so that they shall reach the registrar on or before the fifteenth day of every month, namely, the duplicate of every deed or instrument (except wills and codicils) executed or acknowledged before or attested by him during the preceding month
provisions.why_relevant: Supplies the second of the two further parts. With rule (24) it accounts for the original, the duplicate and the protocol, that is three signed parts of the same tenor and date, which is what the counterpart recital in the testimonium asserts.
provisions.temporal_note: The rule stood as rule (26) in April 2020 and was in force. The only later change is Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(8), which replaced the reference to "Form F" with "Form F 1" later in the same rule; the words quoted here are unaffected.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: Every such attestation shall be substantially in the form E in the Second Schedule, and shall be legibly signed by him in the language in which the deed or instrument is written
provisions.why_relevant: Background, and a boundary marker. The one part of the end of a deed whose form is statutorily prescribed is the notary's attestation, not the testimonium. The question asks only for the testimonium, so Form E material (identification of executants, consideration paid, stamps, erasures) is kept out of the answer.
provisions.temporal_note: Rule (21) unamended by the 2011, 2022 and 2024 amending Acts; in force in April 2020. Form E itself is not held in the corpus.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: an obligation which, if entered into by a natural person is required by law to be in writing signed by that person and be notarially attested, may be entered into on behalf of the company in writing signed under the name of the company by - (i) two directors of the company; (ii) if there be only one director, by that director;
provisions.why_relevant: The lessee is OMEGA (Private) Ltd, a company. A lease of immovable property must be notarially executed, so it falls within paragraph (a): the company executes by signature under the company's name by two directors (or the sole director, or a person or class of persons named in the articles, or an appointed attorney), and the deed must then be notarially executed. This is what the lessee half of the testimonium and the execution block must reflect. The 2007 Act does not require a common seal; s.12(1)(f) treats a company seal as optional.
provisions.temporal_note: Section 19 is unamended and was in force in April 2020. The Companies (Amendment) Act No. 13 of 2019 does not touch it.

provisions.formal_title: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance No. 7 of 1840
provisions.relevant_excerpt: No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other immovable property, and no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for effecting any such object, or for establishing any security, interest, or incumbrance affecting land or other immovable property (other than a lease at will, or for any period not exceeding one month)
provisions.why_relevant: Background: a lease of land for a period exceeding one month is outside the parenthetical exclusion and so must be by notarially attested writing. That is what makes this an indenture of lease attested by a notary at all, and so brings the Notaries Ordinance s.31 duties, and the testimonium's place-and-date recital, into play.
provisions.temporal_note: The words quoted are the opening words of s.2 and were in force in April 2020. Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 30 of 2022 s.2 repealed only the words from "shall be of force" to the end of the section, and Act No. 4 of 2024 s.2 then re-substituted paragraph (a); paragraphs (a) and (b) as they appear in the corpus text therefore post-date the matter and are not relied on. The duration of the proposed lease is not stated in the scenario, so the one-month exclusion cannot be conclusively ruled out on the facts as given.

questions.authority_requirement_reason: The question asks for a drafted clause, and no statute in the corpus prescribes the form or the wording of a testimonium. The Notaries Ordinance prescribes a form only for the notary's attestation (s.31(21), Form E of the Second Schedule), which is a different clause coming after the signatures. What the statutes supply is the content the clause must carry: the place and the date in letters (s.31(18)), execution by the parties before the notary and the witnesses (s.31(12), s.31(8)), the three parts of the deed comprising original, duplicate and protocol (s.31(24), s.31(26)), and the manner in which a company executes a notarially attested instrument (Companies Act s.19(1)(a)). The settled words themselves come from non-statutory conveyancing and notarial practice, which sits outside the frozen statutory corpus, so a complete mark-earning answer cannot be derived from statute alone.

legal_issues.issue: What a testimonium clause in an indenture of lease must recite: the parties, the act of setting their hands, the number of parts executed, the place of execution and the date of execution.
How the lessee, OMEGA (Private) Ltd, a company, is to be recited as executing a notarially attested lease, and whether a common seal must be mentioned.
Whether any statutory form governs the testimonium as distinct from the notary's attestation, and therefore whether the drafted wording can be sourced from the statutory corpus.

questions.hop_count_basis: Three necessary linked steps across two enactments: (1) a lease of land for more than one month must be notarially attested writing (Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2), which (2) engages the notary's execution duties, in particular the recital of place and of the date in letters and execution before the notary (Notaries Ordinance s.31(18) and s.31(12)); and (3) because the lessee is a company, the manner of the lessee's signature must be taken from Companies Act s.19(1)(a). Only these steps are counted; the protocol and duplicate rules refine the counterpart recital but add no required step.

enrichment.original_background:
Anuk de Silva, Pramuk de Silva and Dinuk de Silva are three brothers and they own equal undivided shares of a divided portion of a land in extent of 45 perches as per a Partition Decree in the District Court of Ratnapura in case No. 345/P. Anuk wishes to sell his entitlement of the land. Pramuk wishes to construct a house on his share of the land having mortgaged it to a Bank. Dinuk wants to Lease his share of land to a Company for a commercial purpose. The Bank informed Pramuk that he should have a divided and defined block of land in order to enable them to grant him a loan. Therefore, he informs his brothers that they should file a Partition Action for the division of the property. Anuk has approached you for Legal advice.

Dinuk has requested you to draft an Indenture, of Lease to lease out his block of land after the division of property. The Lessee is OMEGA (Private) Ltd.

gold_answer_draft.issue: Dinuk de Silva is to grant an indenture of lease of his divided block of land to OMEGA (Private) Ltd. The question is how to draft the testimonium clause of that indenture: the clause closing the operative part of the deed, which records that the parties have set their hands to it, in how many parts, at what place and on what date, before the deed passes to the signatures and to the notary's attestation.
gold_answer_draft.rule: A lease of land for a period exceeding one month falls outside the exclusion in the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 for a lease at will or for any period not exceeding one month, and so must be made by writing attested by a notary. That engages the notary's duties under the Notaries Ordinance s.31. Rule (18) obliges the notary to insert in letters in every deed executed before him the day, month and year on which, and the place where, it is executed, so the testimonium must state a place and must spell the date out in words. Rule (12) requires the executants and the witnesses to sign in the presence of the notary and of one another, and rule (8) requires at least two witnesses to subscribe their signatures in letters, so the clause speaks of the parties setting their hands at one place on one date and leads into an execution block with two witness lines. Rules (24) and (26) require the notary to keep a signed protocol and to transmit the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands, so the deed is executed in three parts and the testimonium recites signature hereto and to two others of the same tenor and date as these presents. Because the lessee is a company, Companies Act No. 7 of 2007 s.19(1)(a) governs its signature: an obligation which a natural person would have to make in writing and have notarially attested may be entered into by the company in writing signed under the name of the company by two directors, or by the sole director, or by a person authorised by the articles, or by an appointed attorney, and must then be notarially executed. No common seal is required, the 2007 Act treating a company seal as optional. The wording of the testimonium itself is not statutory; it is settled conveyancing form, and the Notaries Ordinance prescribes a form (Form E, under rule (21)) only for the notary's attestation, a separate clause following the signatures.
gold_answer_draft.application: Dinuk de Silva, the Lessor, executes personally and sets his hand. OMEGA (Private) Ltd, the Lessee, cannot set a hand, so the clause must recite that the company has caused the deed to be signed under its name by two of its directors duly authorised in that behalf, in conformity with s.19(1)(a). The deed will be executed in triplicate, being the original, the duplicate and the protocol, so the parties sign the instrument and two others of the same tenor and date. The place and the date are not given in the scenario; the paper is from the April 2020 session, so the year would be written Two Thousand and Twenty, and the place would in practice be wherever the parties attend on the notary, the land lying in the District of Ratnapura. Those variables are left as blanks in the draft and must be completed at execution, in letters, as rule (18) requires. Matters such as identification of the executants, the consideration and the stamps belong in the notary's attestation under rule (20) and Form E, not in the testimonium, and are deliberately excluded.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The testimonium clause may be drafted as follows: IN WITNESS WHEREOF the said Lessor and the said Lessee have set their hands hereto and to two others of the same tenor and date as these presents at ................ on this ................ day of ................ Two Thousand and Twenty. Where the corporate execution is to be spelt out on the face of the clause, it may read: IN WITNESS WHEREOF the said Lessor Dinuk de Silva has set his hand hereto and the said Lessee OMEGA (Private) Ltd has caused these presents to be signed under its name by two of its Directors duly authorised in that behalf, and to two others of the same tenor and date as these presents, at ................ on this ................ day of ................ Two Thousand and Twenty. The clause is followed by the signature block for the Lessor, the Lessee's two directors and the two witnesses, and then by the notary's attestation. The statutory corpus fixes the content of the clause but not its words, so the precise form above rests on conveyancing practice and is unverified until a lawyer confirms it.

answer_claims.claim_text: A lease of land for a period exceeding one month is not within the exclusion for a lease at will or for a period not exceeding one month, and so must be made by writing attested by a notary.

The notary must correctly insert in letters in every deed executed before him the day, month and year on which, and the place where, it is executed; the testimonium therefore states the place of execution and spells the date in words.

The executants and the witnesses must sign in the presence of the notary and of one another, and the notary must sign in their presence, so the testimonium records a single act of signing at one place on one date.
At least two witnesses must subscribe their signatures in letters to the deed, which is why the execution block following the testimonium carries two witness lines.

Because the notary must preserve a signed protocol and transmit the duplicate of the deed to the Registrar of Lands, the deed is executed in three parts, which is the basis of the recital that the parties set their hands to the instrument and to two others of the same tenor and date.

An obligation which a natural person would have to make in writing and have notarially attested may be entered into on behalf of a company in writing signed under the name of the company by two directors, or by the sole director, or by a person or class of persons authorised by the articles, or by an appointed attorney, and must be notarially executed.

The clause whose form is statutorily prescribed at the end of a deed is the notary's attestation, which must be substantially in Form E of the Second Schedule; the testimonium is a separate clause and no statutory form governs it.

Dinuk de Silva as Lessor sets his hand personally, while the Lessee OMEGA (Private) Ltd must be recited as causing the deed to be signed under its name by two of its directors duly authorised in that behalf; no common seal need be mentioned.

The place and the exact date of execution are not stated in the scenario, so the testimonium leaves them as blanks to be completed in letters at execution; on the April 2020 reference date the year would be written as Two Thousand and Twenty.

The testimonium may accordingly read: IN WITNESS WHEREOF the said Lessor and the said Lessee have set their hands hereto and to two others of the same tenor and date as these presents at ... on this ... day of ... Two Thousand and Twenty.

questions.block_reason: Drafting question whose marks turn on a form of words that no statute in the corpus supplies. The corpus fixes the required content of the clause (place and date in letters under Notaries Ordinance s.31(18); execution before the notary and witnesses under s.31(12) and s.31(8); the original, duplicate and protocol behind the counterpart recital under s.31(24) and s.31(26); corporate execution under Companies Act s.19(1)(a)), but the settled precedent wording of a testimonium comes from non-statutory conveyancing and notarial practice. Reserved as mixed_statute_and_case rather than proposed_gold so a lawyer reviews the drafted wording against a recognised precedent book before it is treated as gold. A secondary open point: the term of the lease is not stated, so the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 one-month exclusion cannot be ruled out on the facts as given.
